definition: Algorithms that defer processing until prediction time, storing data rather than building an explicit model — k-NN and case-based reasoning are the classic examples.
details: Algorithms that defer processing until prediction time, storing data rather than building an explicit model — k-NN and case-based reasoning are the classic examples.

explainer.lead: Lazy learning algorithms store training data and do their work only when a prediction is requested. k-NN and case-based reasoning are the classic examples.

tiers.eli5: Like a cook who keeps every recipe in a drawer and only looks one up when an order comes in.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use them when data arrives incrementally or the decision boundary is irregular; the pitfall is slow prediction and large memory use at query time.
tiers.paperLevel: No explicit model is built during training; generalization is deferred until a query, at which point stored instances are used to produce the answer. Limits include query-time cost that grows with dataset size.

explainer.example: A k-nearest-neighbours recommender stores all past interactions and, at request time, compares the new user against stored ones.
